question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Albuquerque — Conquests and captured territories]
options: Goa — Captured by Albuquerque from the Bijapur Sultanate in 1510
Malacca — Captured by Albuquerque in 1511, giving Portugal control over the Spice Islands trade
Hormuz — Captured by Albuquerque in 1515, controlling the Persian Gulf trade route
Calicut — Captured and made the headquarters of Portuguese India by Albuquerque in 1512
wrong_fact: Calicut was NEVER captured and made headquarters by Albuquerque. Goa (captured 1510) became the permanent capital of Portuguese India, not Calicut. Albuquerque repeatedly failed to capture Calicut; the Zamorin of Calicut remained hostile to the Portuguese.
explanation: Afonso de Albuquerque, the second Governor of Portuguese India, conquered Goa from the Adil Shah of Bijapur in 1510 and made it the permanent capital (headquarters) of Estado da India. He then captured Malacca in 1511 — a key spice trade hub — and Hormuz (on his second attempt) in 1515, controlling the Persian Gulf. Calicut (Kozhikode) remained under the hostile Zamorin and was never fully conquered by Albuquerque.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Albuquerque — Policies and their geographic focus]
options: Policy of intermarriage — Encouraged Portuguese men to marry local women in Goa to create a stable settler population
Ormuz/Hormuz control — Aimed at choking Arab/Muslim trade through the Persian Gulf
Malacca conquest (1511) — Aimed at controlling the sea route to the Moluccas (Spice Islands) in Southeast Asia
Capture of Aden (1513) — Albuquerque successfully captured Aden to control the Red Sea trade, cutting off Ottoman supply lines
wrong_fact: Albuquerque's attempt to capture Aden in 1513 FAILED. He attacked Aden but could not take it due to the strong fortifications. Aden remained outside Portuguese control throughout Albuquerque's tenure.
explanation: Albuquerque's grand strategic design was to control the three key chokepoints of Indian Ocean trade: Hormuz (Persian Gulf), Aden (Red Sea), and Malacca (Strait of Malacca). He succeeded at Hormuz (1515) and Malacca (1511), but his attack on Aden in 1513 failed. He died in 1515 off Goa without having achieved the Red Sea control. His policy of intermarriage (casados) in Goa was a genuine attempt to create a Portuguese-Indian creole settler community.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Albuquerque — Events and associated places/rulers]
options: Battle of Goa (1510) — Albuquerque defeated Yusuf Adil Shah (Bijapur) to capture Goa
Timoja — Hindu privateer chieftain who assisted Albuquerque in the first capture of Goa
Cochin (Kochi) — Friendly port used by the Portuguese as a base before Goa's conquest; Raja Trimumpara allied with Portuguese
Calicut (Kozhikode) — Albuquerque established a permanent fort here (Fort Manuel) as a symbol of Portuguese dominance on the Malabar coast
wrong_fact: Albuquerque did NOT establish a permanent fort at Calicut. The Portuguese fort (Fort Manuel) was established at Cochin (Kochi), not Calicut. The Zamorin of Calicut consistently opposed the Portuguese, and no permanent fort was built there.
explanation: The Portuguese allied with the friendly Raja of Cochin (Trimumpara) and built Fort Manuel (also known as the fort of Cochin) there — their first major fortification on the Malabar coast. Calicut's Zamorin was hostile and the Portuguese were unable to establish a lasting foothold there. Timoja (Thimayya), a Hindu corsair, was instrumental in helping Albuquerque capture Goa from Adil Shah of Bijapur in 1510.
